approach: Add one lexical gate step, `check_environment_reach(reading)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs beside `check_code_survey` (3910), registered as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request));` (3248). It returns Ok when capability is None or a question is set. Three triggers, scanned only in Behavior criteria, the deliverable list and the summary (Content criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope and the request are never scanned, so the repair text cannot trigger its own check). (A) a Create/Modify deliverable under `.github/workflows/`. (B) a host action in a Behavior criterion (git/gh commands, push with a ref target, pull request or `PR` opened/merged/reused, GitHub API calls, CI write verbs). (C1) runtime read of a located source in a Behavior criterion: only the place-naming phrases `records branch`, `athena/records`, `git history`, `git log`, `commit history`, each with a source verb within 3 words before. (C2) the reading's own evidence: a source phrase in the summary (job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, `athena/records`, and the single word `history` but not `history of`), each with a source verb within 3 words before. A, B and C1 are repaired by one `Environment:` assumption naming a site, a permission and a data word (B with a local-type site also needs a no/without/missing-origin case). C2 is repaired by a counted figure quoted in ANY assumption, or an `Environment:` assumption that lists a reachable data/doc file. This answers the new findings: ordinary product wording such as 'computed from the job records' (status.rs:734) or 'Scores a job from its records' (scoring.rs:152) in a Behavior criterion is not a trigger, so the replay share stays small and the C1 repair is a real environment statement, not filler figures. The reader brief gets one rule line, CHANGELOG gets one entry, and the doc comment and CHANGELOG name the root cause and three jobs.

decisions.choice: Split trigger C into C1 (runtime read in a Behavior criterion, place-naming phrases only, repaired by a site/permission/data `Environment:` assumption) and C2 (the reading's own evidence, summary only, repaired by quoted counted figures in any assumption or a reachable file in an `Environment:` assumption). Drop the single word `records` entirely; keep single `history` in the summary only (answers finding 1).
decisions.reason: Reading records is ordinary product behaviour here (status.rs:734, scoring.rs:152, reconcile.rs:59, labeled.rs:29 per the critic's grep). For code that reads records at runtime the real question is where it runs and whether that place has `records/` (the producer snapshot has none, system facts), which the Environment statement answers; demanding '3 jobs' is filler. Figures matter only when the reading's own claims rest on records, which is the nm0k shape (summary). `records branch`, `athena/records` and git history/log name a place that is not in the snapshot, so they alone are C1. Accept fixtures copy the status.rs and scoring.rs wording ('computed from the job records', 'Scores a job from its records', 'reads the records', 'reads records') and must be accepted with no Environment.

rejected.option: Keep single `records` and `history` as Behavior triggers with figure repair
rejected.why: Refuses ordinary product-behaviour criteria and forces filler figures; widens the live replay.

rejected.option: Scan assumptions for C2 as well
rejected.why: The Environment repair text itself names records and history and would trigger its own check.

rejected.option: Require figures for runtime reads too
rejected.why: Quoted figures say nothing about where the code runs or what it reaches.

decisions.choice: State the C2 rule as the reading says it: counted figures quoted in any assumption satisfy it, or an `Environment:` assumption listing a reachable file; no site/permission/data words are required for C2 (answers finding 3). The deviation from criterion 4's literal wording (a records-branch citation in a criterion is repaired by the Environment statement, not by figures) is named in the doc comment and CHANGELOG with the reason: figures cannot describe a runtime read, and data reach (what the site can see) is the root cause.
decisions.reason: Matches the accepted reading's trigger design: case (b) 'alternatively by quoting the figures inline in an assumption'. A year or a bare count of refs is not a figure: digits (1 to 5) must sit directly before job(s), reading(s), commit(s), record(s), run(s), plan(s), introspection(s), attempt(s), case(s) or percent, or before `%`.

rejected.option: Require site, permission and data words plus figures for every records citation
rejected.why: Stricter than the reading and needless for C2; the previous plan did this.

decisions.choice: Cover the PR, GitHub API and CI-write wordings as host-action (B) triggers with case-sensitive `PR`/`PRs` and `CI` tokens, apostrophes removed before tokenising. Use word stems for the PR and pull-request verbs: open, creat, rais, merg, reus, push, submit (so opens, opening, opened, reused, reusing, merged, merges, raised, created all count) (answers finding 5). CI-write verbs: write, writes, written, push, pushes within 3 words after `CI`; `commit`/`commits` count only when they are the word directly after `CI` or after `CI job`/`CI workflow` (answers finding 4), so 'CI checks each commit' and 'CI tests the commits' do not trigger.
decisions.reason: HISTORY.txt:1433 gives job 8ra0's own subject as 'Open the job's PR early at verification start'; lines 906, 1376 and 1453 also use PR. Without these the exact failing shape is accepted. Stems fix the missing forms. Keeping 'commit' as a noun-after-CI trigger would refuse CI reads.

rejected.why: Fires on `pr.rs` and 'gh pr' prose.

rejected.option: Keep commit/commits within 3 words of CI
rejected.why: Noun use after CI is a read, the case the class says is fine.

rejected.option: Fixed verb list without stems

decisions.choice: Tokenise with break markers: remove apostrophes; keep original case per token for `PR`/`CI`; keep backticked spans only for command forms (`git push|fetch|clone|pull|remote`, `gh pr|api|run|auth|workflow|release|issue`) and `athena/records`; bare `api.github.com` is one word; every other backticked span and every bare token with `/`, `_`, `::` or an interior `.` is a Break. Phrase windows never cross a Break.
decisions.reason: Keeps gh/early.rs, `pr.rs`, parse_remote, `push/pull-request/gh` (this job's own criterion 3) and 'originates' from firing; commands in backticks still count.

decisions.choice: Scan Behavior criteria for B and C1, the summary for C2 only, deliverables for A. No empty-deliverable gate; return Ok only on capability None or a question.
decisions.reason: A Behavior criterion is the one that is run, so that is where an action or measurement is assigned (CriterionKind has only Content and Behavior). A measurement-only reading may list no deliverables. The summary is read for C2 only because job nm0k cited records in its summary; this job's summary says 'assumed CI writes' and 'unreachable records' which have no trigger shape.

decisions.choice: Declare 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' as an unmeasured estimate, with basis, and say what the live replay will measure and what the producer should do if it holds (answers finding 2).
decisions.reason: The criterion fixes 8%. Nothing is measured: the snapshot has no records. The narrowed triggers (place-naming phrases only for C1, summary-only for C2, no single `records`) are what keep the share defensible: ordinary product-behaviour wording in Behavior criteria does not trigger. The live replay (run/mod.rs replay_stage 2161, replay_cases 2201/2271, limit 2366) runs the real candidate checker over the newest REPLAY_WINDOW = 50 accepted readings (reading.rs:4083); with a declared 8% the limit is 8 + REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS 5 = 13% (reading.rs:4235, 4378), and `replay_is_held` (4370) holds when newly*100 > total*13, i.e. 7 or more of 50. My estimate, not measured: 2 to 5 of 50 stored readings carry a push/PR/workflow Behavior action or a summary records source (HISTORY.txt shows PR and workflow subjects at lines 906, 1376, 1433, 1453, and 11 workflow-path commits in 200), close to but under the limit.

rejected.why: Nothing was measured.

risks.risk: The live replay (run/mod.rs replay_stage) holds the job if 7 or more of the newest 50 stored accepted readings are newly refused (declared 8% + 5 points = 13%). The 8% is an unmeasured estimate; my own estimate is 2 to 5 of 50, close to the limit.
risks.mitigation: Triggers are narrowed: no single `records` word, C1 only for place-naming phrases, C2 summary only, host actions only in Behavior criteria with verb-plus-target phrases, paths and identifiers skipped. If the hold fires, the send-back lists the readings; the producer reads each, drops or tightens the trigger that fired most (for example the CI-write or GitHub API rule), adds an accept corpus case per false positive and reruns the corpus. The declared 8% is fixed by the criteria and is not edited.

risks.risk: Lexical triggers miss an action in other words or catch a prose mention in a Behavior criterion.
risks.mitigation: Triggers need a verb-plus-target phrase and skip path, identifier and non-command backticked tokens; fixtures pin both sides, including this job's own criteria; the doc comment and CHANGELOG list the missed shapes (a source more than 3 words from its verb, 'counts readings in records', lowercase 'pr' prose) as limits.

risks.risk: Case-sensitive `PR`/`CI` miss lowercase prose, and the single word `history` in the summary can catch an unrelated read.
risks.mitigation: This repository writes 'PR' or 'pull request' (HISTORY.txt:906, 1376, 1433, 1453). Only the summary is scanned for `history`, `history of` is excluded and the repair is one assumption line with a quoted count; the accept fixtures 'the history of the page' and 'written in the records branch' pin the edge.

risks.risk: This job's own accepted summary or criteria hold a phrase that trips the new check.
risks.mitigation: A test copies the criteria and summary from the brief into an accept fixture; traced by hand: criterion 3 `push/pull-request/gh` is a Break, criterion 4 'citing job records, history or the records branch' has no source verb, summary 'assumed CI writes' is not scanned for B and 'unreachable records' has no phrase.

risks.risk: The word lists can be met by a wrong sentence.
risks.mitigation: The check makes the reader state site, permission and data; the doc says it is lexical, as for the `Code survey:` rule. The figure rule needs a counted noun and the file rule excludes records paths and code files.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures that accept workflow-deliverable or action-bearing readings fail once the step exists.
risks.mitigation: Plan step 5 edits the two known tests; the workspace run finds any other, which gets an `Environment:` assumption.

risks.risk: A corpus refuse case is refused by an earlier check (criteria evidence, governance, references) and does not exercise the new step.
risks.mitigation: Workflow cases include a Content criterion naming the workflow path and a request naming no governance path; accept cases use only docs/guide.md and docs/design/roadmap.md from `repo_files()`; the producer checks the refusing check name for each refuse case.

risks.risk: The rule line exceeds the 220-byte cap or the section bound in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: The draft is about 205 bytes with the `- ` prefix; the producer measures it and sets the section bound just above.

risks.risk: New code or comment text trips the boundary scan or the personal-data allow-list.
risks.mitigation: CI and host vocabulary only, no banned phrases, no email-like text; the workspace run includes the scan.

dependents.reason: New text uses CI and host vocabulary only and no email-like text; the workspace run includes the scan.

dependents.name: governance configuration
dependents.reason: The check is a compiled rule in reading.rs. It adds no config key, and no workflow reads the reading rules, so no host setting changes.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs `mod tests` that reads source text. Doc comment: split include_str!("reading.rs") at `pub fn check_environment_reach`, take the contiguous `///` lines before it, strip each leading `///`, collapse white space. CHANGELOG: take include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md") from `## [Unreleased]` to the next `## [` line, split into items at lines starting `- `, collapse white space per item, pick the one item containing 'no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches'. In both texts assert that phrase, '20261024-220048-engm', '20261025-070538-8ra0', '20261025-034247-nm0k', 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 8% of newly refused readings', 'estimate' and 'not measured'.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment and the new CHANGELOG item each name the cause, the three jobs, the intended higher refusal rate and the unmeasured 8% estimate, even when the phrase wraps across lines. Older entries cannot satisfy it.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the doc comment or the CHANGELOG item missing, no item contains the phrase or a needle is absent and the assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: No production function is called; the test reads source text via include_str! of reading.rs and CHANGELOG.md, the same pattern as reading.rs:9142 (exists). The test is added by plan step 5.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) In athena-core take the body of `refusing_check` (split at `pub fn refusing_check(`, as reading.rs:7728 does) and assert `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));` appears exactly once and directly follows `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request));`. (b) In athena-context update `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` (briefs.rs:4400): `READING_RULES.len() == 7`, `check_environment_reach` in its check list, one line holding both `Environment:` and `check_environment_reach`, every line at most 220 bytes, section bound raised just above the measured size.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core environment_reach_has_one_step_line && cargo test -p athena-context the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line
demonstrations.observes: One step line in the stated position, and a reader rule line that tells the reader to write an `Environment:` assumption.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line the count is 0 and (a) fails. Without the rule line the rule count stays 6 and (b) fails.
demonstrations.seam: No production function is called; tests read reading.rs text, the READING_RULES constant (briefs.rs:2225) and the reader brief builder (briefs.rs:2416). All exist; the new assertions are added by plan steps 5 and 7.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_*` in reading.rs `mod tests`, calling `refusing_check` (3226) and `check_environment_reach` directly (guards: capability set, no question). Refuse with no `Environment:` assumption, asserting the refusing check name is `check_environment_reach` and the error starts 'the reading was refused because': (i) Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it; (ii) one Behavior criterion each: 'Athena pushes the job branch to origin', 'The job branch is pushed to the remote', 'A pull request is opened on the remote', 'The pull request is opened with `gh pr create`', a bare `git push` backtick; (iii) "Athena opens the job's PR at verification start", "Open the job's PR early at verification start", 'The early PR is reused by land', 'land calls the GitHub API to reuse the early PR', 'The check calls the GitHub API for the run status', 'The CI job writes the records'. Accept the same readings with 'Environment: the CI job has write permission to refs on the GitHub origin' for CI-site cases; for a local-site case ('the local Athena working copy has write access to the repo; with no origin or a non-GitHub origin it skips the push; with a GitHub origin it can push refs') `refusing_check` returns None. Also: an assumption missing the permission word is refused and the error names 'permissions'; a local-site assumption without the no-origin case is refused; a CI-site assumption without it is accepted; the label matches after trim and in any case; an assumption that only mentions 'environment' does not count; a Delete of a workflow does not trigger. Accept fixtures: Behavior criteria that contain `pr.rs`, gh/early.rs, lowercase 'pr', 'express', 'CIty', 'CI checks each commit' and 'CI tests the commits' do not trigger; 'CI commits the records' does (finding 4).
demonstrations.observes: A workflow deliverable, or a push, pull-request, PR, GitHub API or CI-write action in a Behavior criterion, without a complete `Environment:` assumption is refused by `check_environment_reach`; with one, `refusing_check` gives None. Verb forms opens, opening, reused, merged, raised are all covered (finding 5).
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!` line removed, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the check-name assertions fail. With the label or word lists wrong the accept assertions fail. With the PR/API/CI rules removed the PR and API fixtures are accepted and fail. With 'commit' as a plain word after CI the 'CI checks each commit' accept fixture fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and `check_environment_reach` (the latter added by plan step 4). Fixtures are `Reading` values from `governed_reading` (reading.rs:7364) and `add_behavior` (7505), which exist, plus a `with_environment` helper added in plan step 5. No test double.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_source_*` in reading.rs, each also run through `refusing_check` to assert the refusing check's name. Three readings shaped like the three jobs. (engm, C1 runtime read) a code reading with a `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path (so `check_code_survey` passes) and the Behavior criterion 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch': refused with no Environment assumption; refused with an assumption missing the permission word; accepted with 'Environment: the CI job has read-only access to contents and cannot write the records branch; the producer snapshot has no records/'. (8ra0) the push/origin/PR reading of criterion 3, accepted only with a complete assumption. (nm0k, C2 evidence) a docs reading whose summary says 'Use the figures from job records and history': refused with no assumption; refused when the only Environment file is `records/foo.json`, `athena/records/x.json` or `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`, or the only number is a year; accepted when any assumption quotes '3 jobs' or '40%', or an `Environment:` assumption lists `docs/design/roadmap.md`. Summary 'Use the figures from history' is refused; 'the history of the page' is accepted. Phrase loop: each C1 phrase (records branch, `athena/records` bare and backticked, git history, git log, commit history) with a source verb in a Behavior criterion, and each C2 phrase (job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, athena/records, history) with a source verb in the summary, is refused without the repair. Accept (finding 1 fixtures copied from doc wording): Behavior 'Run `athena status`: rounds per landed job are computed from the job records', 'Scores a job from its records', 'The tool reads the records', 'The audit reads records'; 'The record is written in the records branch'; 'a reading citing job records'; a summary 'The audit counts readings in records' (stated limit). A reading with no deliverables and a records-branch Behavior read is refused.
demonstrations.observes: A reading that reads a located source at runtime is refused unless an Environment statement says where it runs, its permissions and the data reached; a reading whose summary cites records or history as evidence is refused unless counted figures are quoted in an assumption or a reachable file is listed in an Environment assumption; ordinary product wording about reading records is accepted. Three differently shaped readings plus the phrase loops cover the class.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the name assertions fail. Without the figure and file rule, the bare-year and records-only-file readings are wrongly accepted. Without the C1/C2 split, the status.rs and scoring.rs wording fixtures are refused (or the engm shape needs filler figures) and fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and `check_environment_reach`. Fixtures `code_reading` (reading.rs:8936) and `governed_reading` (7364) exist, edited in place; the summary is set on the fixture. No double. The deviation from criterion 4's literal wording is asserted by the C1 accept case and stated in the doc comment.

demonstrations.method: Plan step 6 adds eighteen cases to `reading_check_cases()` (refusal_corpus.rs:668) with `case(..)` and `base_reading` (exist, 186 and 117). Refuse, `Expected::Refuse("check_environment_reach")`: environment-ci-workflow-without-an-environment (Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it), environment-host-action-without-an-environment ('Athena pushes the job branch to origin'), environment-pr-without-an-environment ("Athena opens the job's PR at verification start"), environment-github-api-without-an-environment ('The check calls the GitHub API for the run status'), environment-ci-write-without-an-environment ('The CI job writes the records'), environment-records-branch-read-without-an-environment ('The history check reads the job records on the records branch'), environment-records-summary-without-figures (summary 'Use the figures from job records'), environment-bare-history-summary-without-figures (summary 'Use the figures from history'), environment-records-summary-with-a-bare-year (Environment names only a year). Accept: environment-ci-workflow-with-an-environment, environment-host-action-with-origin-cases, environment-records-branch-read-with-an-environment, environment-records-summary-with-quoted-figures, environment-records-summary-with-a-reachable-file (lists docs/design/roadmap.md, in `repo_files()`), environment-product-reads-records-accepted (status.rs and scoring.rs wording in Behavior criteria, no Environment), environment-trigger-words-only-inside-other-words (dash-bullet request naming push to origin, which becomes Content criteria, plus a Behavior criterion with 'originates', a gh/early.rs path, `parse_remote`, 'entries are pushed onto the list', a Vec push), environment-gh-module-path-only, environment-pr-inside-paths-only (`pr.rs`, gh/early.rs, 'the history of the page', 'written in the records branch'). Input-form map (ids read in the file: code-reading-without-a-survey 689, code-reading-with-a-survey 700, design-reading-without-existing-code 738, request-names-a-governance-file-the-reading-ignores 772, delivery-request-naming-a-workflow-fails-governance-first 393, full-deliverable-path 802, boundary-word-in-a-deliverable-path 890; star-bullets 542, numbered-dot-parts 554): workflow Create/Modify -> the two workflow cases; Delete -> unit test only; push, pull-request, PR, GitHub API, CI-write phrases -> the host-action cases; records-branch runtime read -> the records-branch pair; summary evidence with figure, file, year, bare history -> the summary cases; ordinary product wording -> product-reads-records; slash-joined, path and identifier tokens, words inside other words, PR inside paths -> the accept cases; dash bullets -> the trigger-words case; star and numbered bullets reach the gate only as Content criteria through `base_reading`, which the check does not scan, and are covered by the existing bullet cases. Seven new `INPUT_FORMS` tags: ci-workflow-deliverable, host-action-criterion, records-branch-read, records-evidence-citation, environment-assumption, trigger-word-inside-other-word, pr-or-api-wording (length 23 to 30), each carried by a case. Add `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended`, modelled on `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended` (1102). I have not run the suite and cite no result.
demonstrations.observes: Each case gets its expected outcome, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (1061) and `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` (998) pass because a case refuses with `check_environment_reach` and every tag is carried.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check there is no step line, so `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` (1082) and `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended` fail. With the step present but not firing, the refuse cases fail with 'expected Refuse(check_environment_reach), got accepted'.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (public, used at refusal_corpus.rs:943). Fixtures `Case`, `case()`, `base_reading()` and `repo_files()` exist. Behavior cases replace `reading.acceptance_criteria` in the case body; summary cases set `reading.summary`. Cases are added by plan step 6. No double.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_accepts_*` in reading.rs plus the corpus accept cases. A plain docs reading (`governed_reading(&["docs/x.md"], &["docs/x.md exists"], &[])`) passes `check_environment_reach` and `refusing_check` returns None. Accepted with no `Environment:`: Content criteria naming push, origin, gh/early.rs, parse_remote, PR, 'the history of the page'; Behavior criteria containing only 'fixed where it originates', 'ghost', 'pushdown', 'remotely', 'Vec push', 'entries are pushed onto the list', 'The record is written in the records branch', a `pr.rs` path, status.rs/scoring.rs-style wording 'computed from the job records', 'Scores a job from its records'; this job's own criteria 3 to 7 and its summary copied from the brief; a push or PR phrase in an assumption or in out_of_scope only; a decline (capability None); a reading with a question. The 8% estimate is pinned by the criterion 1 and 5 declaration tests, and the replay declaration is checked with `replay_declaration_of` returning share Some(8) for this job's criterion text.
demonstrations.observes: Docs-only readings and readings without an assigned action or located-source read are accepted. Words in paths, identifiers, Content criteria and other words do not trigger.
demonstrations.fails_without: With substring or bare-token triggers, 'originates', gh/early.rs and parse_remote are refused and the accept tests fail. With single `records` as a Behavior trigger the status.rs wording is refused and fails. Without the capability and question guards the decline and question readings are refused.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `check_environment_reach` (new) and `refusing_check` (exists). Fixtures `governed_reading` (7364) and `add_behavior` (7505) exist; Behavior criteria are set by editing the criterion kind in place. No double.

demonstrations.method: Run the three commands. The full workspace run is needed because `check_reading_text` (reading.rs:4128) is shared by the steward, the CLI check-reading command, run/tests.rs and drain.rs, and because workspace tests include the boundary scan and the budgets test. Any fixture elsewhere that the new rule refuses gets an `Environment:` assumption; the check is never weakened. Also at verification the live replay (run/mod.rs replay_stage) runs the new checker over up to 50 stored accepted readings: limit 13% with the declared 8%, hold at 7 or more newly refused of 50. If it holds, the send-back lists the readings; the producer reads each, tightens the trigger that fired most or adds a verb/phrase exclusion plus an accept corpus case, and does not weaken the A/B/C rules wholesale.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets && cargo test --workspace
demonstrations.fails_without: A fixture reading in another crate that trips the new check fails `cargo test --workspace`. A briefs.rs array length or size bound left at 6 or 2400 fails the briefs tests.
demonstrations.seam: The workspace build and test commands themselves; no fixture of my own. The replay is run by Athena at verification, not by this command.

open_questions: User: criterion 4 says a reading citing records or history is refused unless figures are quoted or a reachable file is listed. The plan applies that to the reading's own evidence (summary) and asks for a site/permission/data `Environment:` statement instead for a Behavior criterion that reads the records branch or git history at runtime, because figures cannot describe a runtime read. Confirm this reading of criterion 4.
